Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Sep 16, 4:10PM CDT
The latest update is out from Charter Communications ( (CHTR) ).
On September 15, 2026, Charter Communications announced that its board declared a regular quarterly cash dividend for holders of its Series A Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock. The dividend was set at $0.43750001 per share, payable in cash on October 15, 2026 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on September 30, 2026.

The announcement underscores Charter’s ongoing capital-return commitments to preferred shareholders and clarifies the terms and schedule of distributions tied to the Liberty Broadband acquisition.

SpaceX logo on smartphone with a rocket taking off in the background (Credit: Image via Shutterstock)
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:31 AM PDT 5 min read
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Space Exploration Technologies Corp. could pose a growing threat to terrestrial broadband providers, particularly in rural and lower-density markets, MoffettNathanson analyst Craig Moffett said Tuesday as Starlink begins deploying higher-capacity V3 satellites.
Starlink Poses Bigger Threat to Comcast and Charter
The analyst sees SpaceX's Starlink becoming a more credible competitor to terrestrial broadband as Starship enables higher-capacity satellite deployments, although he expects fiber and cable networks to retain important speed advantages.
Moffett told CNBC that Starlink presents a much greater competitive challenge to terrestrial broadband providers such as Comcast Corp. and Charter Communications Inc. than to traditional wireless carriers such as AT&T Inc. and Verizon Communications Inc..

"The terrestrial broadband business where they deliver ISP service is a very credible product and will have a direct impact. It already is having a significant impact," Moffett said.
Investors are now trying to determine whether Starlink's impact will remain concentrated in rural and low-density markets or expand further into suburban and potentially some urban areas.
Moffett said the technology remains best suited to rural markets but can also serve some customers in denser areas.
V3 Satellites Strengthen Starlink's Offering
SpaceX's first Starship orbital flight marked an important milestone because the rocket deployed 26 V3 Starlink satellites, which Moffett said carry substantially more capacity and should improve the service.
However, he expects the transition to take time. Moffett said it will be after 2030 before most of the Starlink constellation consists of V3 satellites.

Even with V3 satellites, he does not expect Starlink to match the speeds offered by terrestrial fiber or cable broadband.
That leaves pricing and customer segmentation as major competitive factors. Starlink could compete more effectively for value-oriented customers who prioritize lower costs over maximum broadband performance.
Moffett compared Starlink's challenge with the pressure Comcast and Charter already face from fixed wireless access.
The cable operators have responded by bundling broadband with wireless services, a strategy Moffett said has proven relatively successful.
The key question is how far Starlink can expand beyond its natural strength in rural markets and take customers from traditional broadband providers without matching the speed and quality of fiber and cable networks.

SpaceX’s Starlink Just Got More Powerful, and Cable Giants Comcast, Charter May Feel the Heat
SpaceX logo on smartphone with a rocket taking off in the background (Credit: Image via Shutterstock)
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:31 AM PDT 5 min read
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Space Exploration Technologies Corp. could pose a growing threat to terrestrial broadband providers, particularly in rural and lower-density markets, MoffettNathanson analyst Craig Moffett said Tuesday as Starlink begins deploying higher-capacity V3 satellites.
Starlink Poses Bigger Threat to Comcast and Charter
The analyst sees SpaceX's Starlink becoming a more credible competitor to terrestrial broadband as Starship enables higher-capacity satellite deployments, although he expects fiber and cable networks to retain important speed advantages.
Moffett told CNBC that Starlink presents a much greater competitive challenge to terrestrial broadband providers such as Comcast Corp. and Charter Communications Inc. than to traditional wireless carriers such as AT&T Inc. and Verizon Communications Inc..

"The terrestrial broadband business where they deliver ISP service is a very credible product and will have a direct impact. It already is having a significant impact," Moffett said.
Investors are now trying to determine whether Starlink's impact will remain concentrated in rural and low-density markets or expand further into suburban and potentially some urban areas.
Moffett said the technology remains best suited to rural markets but can also serve some customers in denser areas.
V3 Satellites Strengthen Starlink's Offering
SpaceX's first Starship orbital flight marked an important milestone because the rocket deployed 26 V3 Starlink satellites, which Moffett said carry substantially more capacity and should improve the service.
However, he expects the transition to take time. Moffett said it will be after 2030 before most of the Starlink constellation consists of V3 satellites.
See Also: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time
Even with V3 satellites, he does not expect Starlink to match the speeds offered by terrestrial fiber or cable broadband.
That leaves pricing and customer segmentation as major competitive factors. Starlink could compete more effectively for value-oriented customers who prioritize lower costs over maximum broadband performance.
Moffett compared Starlink's challenge with the pressure Comcast and Charter already face from fixed wireless access.
The cable operators have responded by bundling broadband with wireless services, a strategy Moffett said has proven relatively successful.
The key question is how far Starlink can expand beyond its natural strength in rural markets and take customers from traditional broadband providers without matching the speed and quality of fiber and cable networks.

Entertainment franchises can become valuable long-term assets when they successfully expand across multiple platforms. Skybound Entertainment, the company behind The Walking Dead and Invincible, develops original intellectual property that spans comics, television, film, video games, merchandise, and licensing. With more than 250 IPs in its portfolio and a strategy focused on retaining franchise rights while scaling successful stories across media, Skybound offers investors exposure to the growing entertainment and creator economy through a private company rather than traditional public market investments.
Coffee is a daily staple for millions of consumers, but investors rarely get direct exposure to the brands and supply chains behind it. With the brand expanding across major retailers including Target, Walgreens and Kroger, and GCC reporting 26X revenue growth over four years, the company is positioning itself to bring a well-known Colombian coffee brand to more consumers across North America.
As artificial intelligence drives a surge in electricity demand, reliable power generation is becoming a critical part of the technology ecosystem. American PowerGen is developing natural gas-fired power plants in Texas, a fast-growing market fueled by AI data centers, manufacturing expansion, and population growth. By advancing projects through permitting, fuel supply, and grid interconnection, the company is positioning itself to help meet rising energy needs while offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting the next wave of AI and industrial growth.
As electricity demand rises alongside AI, data centers, and renewable energy, long-duration energy storage is becoming increasingly important. Qnetic is developing a kinetic energy storage system designed to provide long-lasting, chemical-free electricity storage, offering investors exposure to the infrastructure supporting a more resilient and reliable power grid.
For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and bonds, EquityMultiple provides access to vetted commercial real estate deals starting at $5,000, with only ~5% of opportunities passing their due diligence process.
Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds. For accredited investors, FarmTogether offers direct access to high-quality U.S. farmland starting at $15,000 — fully managed, with no landlord headaches.
Private real estate and private credit can add income and stability to a stock-heavy portfolio. Spectrum's plan to activate AI capable computing across more than 1,000 embedded edge facilities gives Charter Communications (CHTR) a fresh angle on its broadband footprint, as investors reassess a sharply weaker year to date share performance.
Charter Communications has been rolling out these edge AI partnerships just as sentiment has weakened, with the share price down 27.96% over the past 30 days and 47.12% year to date, while the 1 year total shareholder return has fallen 59.77%. Charter Communications Sees Higher Broadband Losses, Better Financial Trends, UBS Says
Mon, September 28, 2026 at 11:49 AM PDT 1 min read
Charter Communications' (CHTR) Q3 results should show steeper broadband subscriber losses even as financial metrics improve modestly, as rate actions in broadband and higher political ad spending help offset persistent competitive pressure from fiber and convergence, UBS Securities said in a note Monday.
The investment firm said its estimates exclude Cox, following the transaction's Aug. 20 closing, and will be updated once trending schedules are provided in mid-October. It attributed the expected pickup in broadband losses to fiber and convergence competition, with satellite also set to grow as Starlink expands its V3 constellation.
UBS said video should continue to outperform in the market, mobile net adds should slow year-over-year, and residential revenue trends should improve as July pricing actions take hold.
For 2027, UBS expects Cox to see accelerating declines while legacy Charter trends remain similar, with over $1 billion of cost synergies expected within three years of close.
UBS has a neutral rating on the stock with a price target of $140.

CHARTER ANNOUNCES CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER TRANSITION
Stamford, CT. – Aug. 31, 2026 – Charter Communications (NASDAQ: CHTR) today announced that Jessica Fischer will
step down from her current position as the Company’s Chief Financial Officer on October 15, to relocate for another professional opportunity. The Company will begin a comprehensive search for her
replacement immediately.
Charter also named Kevin Howard, currently Executive Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer & Controller, to the position of interim Chief Financial Officer
effective October 15. Mr. Howard will continue to work closely with Ms. Fischer to support ongoing financial operations and ensure a seamless leadership transition.
“I first met Jessica more than 15 years ago and actively recruited her to join our team at Charter,” said Chris Winfrey, President & CEO, Charter Communications.
“Since joining Charter nearly 10 years ago, and becoming our CFO in 2021, she has been a key part of our executive team. I am very proud of our work together and grateful for her many contributions in making Spectrum the leading broadband and video
“It has been a privilege to be part of Charter’s growth over the past decade,” said Ms. Fischer. “I have learned so much from Chris and this team and am grateful for the
opportunity and trust they placed in me to lead Charter’s financial operation.”
Mr. Howard brings over two decades of financial leadership to his role as Charter’s Executive Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer & Controller, overseeing
accounting, tax, financial reporting, and ERP operations. He has led the financial integration of a number of Charter’s major transactions, including the acquisitions of Bresnan, Time Warner Cable, Bright House Networks and Cox Communications. He
previously served as Charter’s interim CFO in 2010.
Charter has not changed any of its previously provided financial outlook or financial policy.
Charter Communications, Inc. (NASDAQ: CHTR) is the leading broadband and video company in the nation and the fastest growing mobile provider in its
footprint, with services available to more than 70 million homes and small to large businesses across 45 states through its Spectrum brand. Founded in 1993, Charter has evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a
converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience. Over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by our 100% U.S.-based employees, the Company offers Seamless Connectivity and Entertainment with Spectrum Internet®, Mobile, TV and Voice
products.
More information can be found at corporate.charter.com.
Media Contact:
Cameron Blanchard, cameron.blanchard@spectrum.com
Investor Relations:
Stefan Anninger, stefan.annigner@charter.com

Jabil Inc. Earnings Call: AI Boom Fuels 2027 Outlook
Tipranks - Tipranks - Fri Oct 2, 7:08PM CDT
Jabil Inc. ((JBL)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Jabil Inc. struck a decidedly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call as management showcased record fourth-quarter execution and robust growth plans stretching into fiscal 2027. Executives acknowledged pockets of softness and operational friction, yet emphasized accelerating AI demand, improving margins and strong free cash flow as key drivers of confidence in the company’s long-term trajectory.
Fourth-Quarter Surge in Revenue and Earnings
Jabil delivered a powerful finish to fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter revenue around $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above its June outlook midpoint. Core operating income reached $675 million and core diluted EPS climbed 34% to $4.40, with both revenue and EPS surpassing the high end of guidance, underscoring strong execution across the portfolio.
Fiscal 2026: Broad-Based Growth and Cash Generation
For the full year, revenue grew 21% and core operating margin expanded by 40 basis points, signaling better pricing, mix and efficiency. Core EPS increased 34%, while adjusted free cash flow exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than $200 million, reinforcing the benefits of Jabil’s asset-light manufacturing model and disciplined capital spending.
Intelligent Infrastructure Drives Outperformance
Intelligent Infrastructure was the standout segment in the quarter, posting revenue of roughly $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and about $900 million ahead of June expectations. Management highlighted that AI-related demand is not only strong but accelerating, as capacity came online faster than planned and customer ramps progressed better than anticipated.
Margin Improvement in Intelligent Infrastructure
Core operating margin in Intelligent Infrastructure reached 6.5%, an increase of 60 basis points from a year earlier. This improvement reflects a more favorable business mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition, which management described as margin-accretive and strategically aligned with Jabil’s data center and power solutions.
Rapid Expansion and Diversification of AI Revenue
AI-related revenue hit approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, rising $5.4 billion from the prior year as hyperscale and cloud customers stepped up orders. Jabil expects AI-related revenue to surge another 54% to about $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, with four customers already above $1 billion in annual AI sales and six Intelligent Infrastructure customers forecast to exceed that threshold next year.
Broad-Based Intelligent Infrastructure Growth Outlook
Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Intelligent Infrastructure revenue is projected at roughly $25.6 billion, about 43% higher than in 2026, with all three end markets growing at double-digit rates. Capital equipment revenue is expected to rise about 40% to $4.2 billion, cloud and data center infrastructure about 52% to $17.5 billion and networking and communications about 15% to $3.9 billion.
Global Capacity Expansion to Meet Committed Demand
To support its growth, Jabil added roughly 4 million square feet of capacity across Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India, targeting high-demand markets and strategic customers. Management stressed that committed business is already filling this footprint and that ongoing customer ramps and new capacity coming online will underpin the company’s fiscal 2027 growth trajectory.
Regulated Industries Growth and Portfolio Upgrades
Regulated Industries delivered solid growth, with fourth-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year and above guidance, helped by stronger automotive, transportation and energy infrastructure demand. For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects the segment to reach about $13.6 billion, up around 7%, with mid-single to high-single digit growth across automotive, healthcare, packaging and renewable energy.
Strategic Repositioning in Automotive Mix
Automotive returned to growth faster than expected, driven by stronger operational execution and better win rates with strategic customers. The business has shifted away from heavy exposure to electrification and powertrain, which fell from about 80% of the portfolio in fiscal 2023 to around 40% in fiscal 2026, with software-defined vehicles, vehicle compute and advanced driver assistance now constituting much of the balance.
Defense, Aerospace and Healthcare Build Momentum
Defense and aerospace are poised to become more meaningful contributors in fiscal 2027 as several programs transition from development into production. Healthcare is expected to resume growth as clients launch new products and engage Jabil for complex manufacturing, with the company planning to produce more than 700 million injectors and pens and ramp its Croatia facility through 2027 into full production in fiscal 2028.
Expanding Footprint in Energy Infrastructure
Renewable and energy infrastructure conditions improved through fiscal 2026, with investment expanding beyond solar into storage, grid solutions and thermal management. Jabil is channeling capital into engineering, vertical integration and selective deals in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear, positioning the company as a broader partner in decarbonization and data center cooling.
Shift Toward Intelligent Devices and Robotics
The company rebranded its Connected Living & Digital Commerce operations as Intelligent Devices & Robotics to reflect a pivot toward automation and complex engineered solutions. Within this segment, Commerce & Robotics is expected to deliver about $3 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, up roughly 11%, fueled by retailer and warehouse investment in robotic systems and automated fulfillment.
Robotics Production and Physical AI Capabilities
Jabil’s customer Symbotic reached 10,000 bots as of June 2025 and is closing in on 20,000 units, demonstrating the scale of automated warehouse deployments. Jabil is also applying its know-how in optics, robotics, precision mechanics, sensors and thermal solutions to humanoid robots and industrial automation, laying the groundwork for broader physical AI applications.
Investments in Operational Automation and Factory Efficiency
Management is investing heavily in factory automation, material movement, computer vision and automated optical inspection to enhance manufacturing performance. These physical AI capabilities are designed to improve consistency, speed up program ramps, detect issues earlier and make equipment more reusable, boosting productivity and resilience as demand shifts.
Robust Cash Flow and Asset-Light Discipline
Cash from operations reached $733 million in the quarter and about $2 billion for fiscal 2026, while net capital expenditures remained modest at $470 million, or 1.3% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5 billion, and Jabil expects net capex of 1.5% to 2% of revenue in fiscal 2027, with adjusted free cash flow around $1.6 billion, underscoring its asset-light approach.
Structural Improvement in Profitability and Returns
Since fiscal 2020, Jabil has steadily improved its profitability, lifting core operating margin from 3.2% to 5.8% and gross margin by more than 200 basis points to 9.2%. Net capital spending has dropped from 2.9% to 1.3% of revenue, annual free cash flow has more than tripled to $1.5 billion and core ROIC has nearly tripled to 59%, signaling stronger returns on invested capital.
Strong Balance Sheet and Shareholder-Friendly Policy
The company ended fiscal 2026 with debt to core EBITDA of 1.3x, cash of about $1.7 billion and total liquidity of $6.1 billion, including $4.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity. Jabil repurchased around $1.1 billion of shares during the year, has cut its share count by 49% since 2013 and is working under a new $1.5 billion buyback plan, aiming to return at least 80% of adjusted free cash flow to investors over time.
Segment-Level Challenges and Strategic Trade-Offs
Not all areas met expectations, with healthcare and packaging revenue falling short in the quarter due to delayed automation equipment and program timing. Connected Living & Digital Commerce revenue was roughly flat year-over-year at $1.4 billion and is projected to decline about 15% to $2.3 billion in fiscal 2027, outweighing Commerce & Robotics growth and leaving Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 2% overall.
Prioritizing Profitability in Intelligent Devices & Robotics
The Intelligent Devices & Robotics segment is expected to generate about $1.2 billion in first-quarter revenue, down roughly 10% year-over-year as Jabil shifts focus from volume to returns. Management said it has exited or deemphasized lower-margin programs that failed to meet its hurdle rates, accepting near-term top-line pressure to safeguard segment profitability.
Inventory Management and Supply Constraints
Net inventory days improved by about four days sequentially to 64, though still above the target range of 55 to 60 days, reflecting higher commodity prices and greater deposits tied to cloud infrastructure. Memory supply is being redirected toward AI and hyperscale demand, and Jabil expects to navigate ongoing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions, acknowledging potential bumps as fiscal 2027 unfolds.
Ramp-Related Margin Pressure and Seasonal Headwinds
Management cautioned that fiscal 2027 revenue will be weighted 45% to the first half and 55% to the second half, with income more back-end loaded as new programs ramp. Initial ramp costs, lower yields and underutilization could compress margins in the first half, while the broader communications market remains subdued and second-quarter revenue faces typical post-holiday seasonality.
Despite heavy investment in physical AI, management noted that real-world deployments remain minimal, particularly in Western markets. Jabil has built a modest, conservative physical AI forecast into its fiscal 2027 outlook, viewing the space as a longer-term opportunity rather than a near-term growth engine.
Monitoring External Macro and Regulatory Risks
The company continues to monitor geopolitical tensions, inflation, supply-chain issues and potential regulatory changes that could affect operations. While no major regulatory disruption is assumed in fiscal 2027, Jabil remains cautious about possible inflection points tied to upcoming elections and broader macro uncertainty.
Guidance Highlights: Strong Growth, Margin Expansion
For the first quarter, Jabil expects total revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion, with Regulated Industries up about 12%, Intelligent Infrastructure up roughly 63% and Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 10%. For fiscal 2027, the company guides to revenue of about $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin of 6.1%, core EPS of $17.55, adjusted free cash flow near $1.6 billion and net capex at 1.5% to 2% of revenue.
Jabil’s latest earnings call painted the picture of a company riding a powerful AI and infrastructure wave while steadily tightening its capital and cost discipline. Despite near-term margin and segment pressures, management’s confident guidance, structural profitability gains and ongoing shareholder returns will likely keep the stock on the radar of investors seeking exposure to the hardware backbone of the AI boom.

The engine is AI infrastructure. Jabil generated $14.4 billion of AI-related revenue in fiscal 2026 and expects $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, a 54% increase. What makes that easier to believe is where the demand comes from. Management says most of it supports inference, the everyday running of existing models, rather than the race to train frontier systems, and direct exposure to frontier developers is a small fraction. Usage-driven demand needs storage, networking, power, and cooling, not just accelerators, and Jabil now builds across all of it. Six customers in the segment are expected to top $1 billion each in fiscal 2027.
The second leg is how efficiently growth turns into cash. Jabil supported $36.0 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026 on just $470 million of net capital spending, which is why core return on invested capital sits at 59%, nearly triple the fiscal 2020 level. Free cash flow beat the company's own early target, and management plans to return at least 80% of it to shareholders over time. Buybacks absorbed about $1.1 billion of that in fiscal 2026.
Growth at this pace has to be physically built, and supply is the choke point. Francis McKay, the chief supply chain officer, said memory is being pulled toward AI and hyperscale buyers, squeezing the other markets Jabil serves. That already shows up in guidance, where Connected Living is expected to shrink 15% to $2.3 billion, partly because management is cautious about memory and partly because it is exiting lower-complexity programs. Healthcare also fell short of expectations in the fourth quarter, thanks to equipment delays and a customer program that slipped.
Execution and concentration come next. Is that caution fair? An inference-heavy mix and a share count cut by 49% since fiscal 2013 argue for some support under the stock. But a modest multiple only looks cheap if the earnings arrive, and memory supply and the capacity buildout are the two things that could delay them.
Jabil's story comes down to whether its new factory space fills on schedule. The evidence shows a company growing fast, generating cash and trading at a multiple that does not demand perfection. Bulls need committed customer programs to keep ramping into the capacity already built. Bears need only a memory shortage or a stumbled launch to show how much.

Jabil Inc. (JBL) reported stronger fiscal 2026 results as revenue growth and higher margins supported its next growth phase. The company posted $36 billion in annual revenue, up 21%, while setting a $44.5 billion sales target for fiscal 2027. Shares closed at $318.84, down 0.03%, before falling to $310.21 in pre-market trading.
Jabil Reports Strong Fiscal 2026 Results
Jabil recorded fourth-quarter revenue of $10.6 billion for fiscal 2026. The company generated U.S. GAAP operating income of $602 million during the quarter. It also delivered diluted earnings per share of $3.76 under U.S. GAAP.
Jabil reported core operating income of $675 million in the fourth quarter. The company posted core diluted earnings per share of $4.40 during the period. These figures reflected stronger operational performance across multiple business areas.
For the full fiscal year, Jabil achieved U.S. GAAP operating income of $1.7 billion. The company recorded U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share of $9.75. It also generated core operating income of $2.1 billion and core diluted earnings per share of $13.09.
Jabil expanded its operations through increased customer demand and new production capacity. The company supported growth across automotive, healthcare, energy infrastructure, defense, aerospace, and automation markets. It also increased its focus on engineering and manufacturing services.
The company generated more than $1.5 billion in adjusted free cash flow during fiscal 2026. Furthermore, Jabil maintained a strategy focused on improving efficiency and expanding customer relationships. The company continued investing in capabilities to support future demand.
Jabil Targets $44.5 Billion Fiscal 2027 Revenue
Jabil expects fiscal 2027 revenue to reach $44.5 billion. The company projects core operating margin at 6.1% for the upcoming fiscal year. It also forecasts core diluted earnings per share of $17.55.
For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Jabil expects revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion. The company projects U.S. GAAP operating income between $481 million and $541 million. It also expects U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share between $2.78 and $3.18.
Jabil forecasts first-quarter core operating income between $592 million and $652 million. The company expects core diluted earnings per share between $3.80 and $4.20. These estimates include adjustments for several non-GAAP expenses.
Jabil expects adjusted free cash flow to reach about $1.6 billion in fiscal 2027. The company plans to use its financial strength to support expansion and shareholder returns. It also expects continued demand from technology infrastructure projects.
The company’s fiscal 2027 outlook reflects continued growth from advanced manufacturing services. Jabil supports customers across several industries requiring complex supply chains. The company has expanded its role by providing design, engineering, and production solutions.
Jabil’s latest results highlight its stronger financial position after a year of revenue growth. The company continues building capacity while maintaining profitability targets. The fiscal 2027 forecast places focus on further expansion and operational improvement.

Jabil’s Double-Beat and Raise Is a Signal That This Rally Will Continue
Thomas Hughes - MarketBeat - Thu Oct 1, 8:45AM CDT
Tepid market response or not, Jabil’s (NYSE: JBL) recent double-beat earnings report was a buy signal, reinforcing the thesis that has driven shares thus far and strengthening the forward outlook.
AI is driving a surge in demand across the company's product lines, pointing to a sustained upcycle and cash-generating capacity.
Cash-generating capacity is the core thesis, as Jabil is the muscle behind more prominent names such as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), and Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ), converting demand for their products into reality.
Jabil’s dividend is a token, yielding less than 0.25%, intended mainly to keep dividend-only funds and institutions in the mix. The firm aggressively repurchases shares and can continue doing so next year.
Highlights from its last fiscal year include about $1 billion in repurchases, up year over year and sufficient to reduce the share count by 3.6%, and a free cash flow payout ratio of about 69%.
Looking ahead, management forecasts free cash flow growth in the coming year, signaling capacity for accelerated buybacks and greater shareholder leverage, which may provide an incentive to buy shares at current levels.
Jabil Boosted by AI, Shows Strengths in All Categories
Jabil posted a solid quarter, with revenue accelerating sequentially and year over year (YOY) to nearly 29%, the fastest pace in more than five years. Revenue growth also outpaced the consensus by a wide margin, approximately 900 basis points (bps), driven by 56% growth in Intelligent Infrastructure. Intelligent Infrastructure did the heavy lifting, but was not the only segment to show strength, with Regulated Industries up by 9% and Connected Living/Digital Commerce flat. CEO Mike Dastoor also highlighted several end markets not related to the data center and AI infrastructure, including automotive, healthcare, energy, defense, aerospace, and warehouse automation.
Margin news was another bright spot. The company faced cost pressures and gross margin headwinds, but they were less than expected and offset by operational quality. Selling, general, and administrative expenses increased at a much slower pace than revenue growth, showing that Jabil is becoming more efficient as it grows, which helped earnings rise faster than revenue. Adjusted earnings per share rose nearly 34% YOY to $4.40, outpacing top-line growth by about 500 bps, with strengths expected to carry into the coming year.
Guidance is a key reason the stock price uptrend is likely to continue. Jabil’s guidance for the next quarter and year is hot on all counts, with revenue and earnings expected to be well above MarketBeat’s reported consensus. The likely outcome is that JBL continues to build momentum, running at the high end of its expected range if not exceeding it, and lifting the year-end outlook along the way.
Analysts Caution Triggers Buying Opportunity in Jabil Shares
Analysts were generally bullish following Jabil’s release, highlighting the revenue strength and earnings quality, but took a cautious stance, focusing on back-end margin expansion and the upfront cost of its capacity buildout. No analysts revised a price target or altered sentiment immediately following the report, leaving the trend unchanged.
The trend includes steady coverage, a Buy consensus with 90% Buy-side bias, and a forecast for nearly 50% upside relative to Q3’s support levels and a fresh all-time high. More importantly, JBL trades well below the lowest analyst price target, signaling a deep-value opportunity and potential for explosive upside as stronger catalysts emerge.
Institutions are likewise bullish on Jabil's stock, citing its cash flow, capital returns, and underlying demand for its clients' products. They own more than 90% of the shares, have bought aggressively over the trailing 12 months, and ramped activity in Q3, reaching a record peak.
JBL’s price action reflects a bullish market posture. The stock is up more than 35% YOY and more than 100% over the past two years, with the 2026 pullback offering value relative to recent peaks. A deeper pullback is possible, but strong support is evident as September comes to a close, so the risk is minimal. The likely scenario is that JBL remains close to this level until more news becomes available, likely in upcoming earnings reports.
The market may not be getting JBL’s report wrong so much as the price action reflects the split between short-term traders and long-term investors. Short-term traders focus on near-term bottlenecks, AI fears, and capacity costs, and fail to price in the impact on long-term cash flow. Long-term traders, focused on cash flow, capital returns, and capital gains, can easily look past upfront costs and focus on the demand curve, which is improving quarterly across numerous end markets, not just AI.
Jabil’s biggest risk now is executional. Investors need the company's strategy to progress without hiccups, which are likely, given the advanced nature of AI hardware and industry-wide bottlenecks.

Jabil Inc. Earnings Call: AI Boom Fuels 2027 Outlook
Tipranks - Tipranks - Fri Oct 2, 7:08PM CDT
Jabil Inc. ((JBL)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Jabil Inc. struck a decidedly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call as management showcased record fourth-quarter execution and robust growth plans stretching into fiscal 2027. Executives acknowledged pockets of softness and operational friction, yet emphasized accelerating AI demand, improving margins and strong free cash flow as key drivers of confidence in the company’s long-term trajectory.
Fourth-Quarter Surge in Revenue and Earnings
Jabil delivered a powerful finish to fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter revenue around $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above its June outlook midpoint. Core operating income reached $675 million and core diluted EPS climbed 34% to $4.40, with both revenue and EPS surpassing the high end of guidance, underscoring strong execution across the portfolio.
Fiscal 2026: Broad-Based Growth and Cash Generation
For the full year, revenue grew 21% and core operating margin expanded by 40 basis points, signaling better pricing, mix and efficiency. Core EPS increased 34%, while adjusted free cash flow exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than $200 million, reinforcing the benefits of Jabil’s asset-light manufacturing model and disciplined capital spending.
Intelligent Infrastructure Drives Outperformance
Intelligent Infrastructure was the standout segment in the quarter, posting revenue of roughly $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and about $900 million ahead of June expectations. Management highlighted that AI-related demand is not only strong but accelerating, as capacity came online faster than planned and customer ramps progressed better than anticipated.
Margin Improvement in Intelligent Infrastructure
Core operating margin in Intelligent Infrastructure reached 6.5%, an increase of 60 basis points from a year earlier. This improvement reflects a more favorable business mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition, which management described as margin-accretive and strategically aligned with Jabil’s data center and power solutions.
Rapid Expansion and Diversification of AI Revenue
AI-related revenue hit approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, rising $5.4 billion from the prior year as hyperscale and cloud customers stepped up orders. Jabil expects AI-related revenue to surge another 54% to about $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, with four customers already above $1 billion in annual AI sales and six Intelligent Infrastructure customers forecast to exceed that threshold next year.
Broad-Based Intelligent Infrastructure Growth Outlook
Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Intelligent Infrastructure revenue is projected at roughly $25.6 billion, about 43% higher than in 2026, with all three end markets growing at double-digit rates. Capital equipment revenue is expected to rise about 40% to $4.2 billion, cloud and data center infrastructure about 52% to $17.5 billion and networking and communications about 15% to $3.9 billion.
Global Capacity Expansion to Meet Committed Demand
To support its growth, Jabil added roughly 4 million square feet of capacity across Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India, targeting high-demand markets and strategic customers. Management stressed that committed business is already filling this footprint and that ongoing customer ramps and new capacity coming online will underpin the company’s fiscal 2027 growth trajectory.
Regulated Industries Growth and Portfolio Upgrades
Regulated Industries delivered solid growth, with fourth-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year and above guidance, helped by stronger automotive, transportation and energy infrastructure demand. For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects the segment to reach about $13.6 billion, up around 7%, with mid-single to high-single digit growth across automotive, healthcare, packaging and renewable energy.
Strategic Repositioning in Automotive Mix
Automotive returned to growth faster than expected, driven by stronger operational execution and better win rates with strategic customers. The business has shifted away from heavy exposure to electrification and powertrain, which fell from about 80% of the portfolio in fiscal 2023 to around 40% in fiscal 2026, with software-defined vehicles, vehicle compute and advanced driver assistance now constituting much of the balance.
Defense, Aerospace and Healthcare Build Momentum
Defense and aerospace are poised to become more meaningful contributors in fiscal 2027 as several programs transition from development into production. Healthcare is expected to resume growth as clients launch new products and engage Jabil for complex manufacturing, with the company planning to produce more than 700 million injectors and pens and ramp its Croatia facility through 2027 into full production in fiscal 2028.
Expanding Footprint in Energy Infrastructure
Renewable and energy infrastructure conditions improved through fiscal 2026, with investment expanding beyond solar into storage, grid solutions and thermal management. Jabil is channeling capital into engineering, vertical integration and selective deals in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear, positioning the company as a broader partner in decarbonization and data center cooling.
Shift Toward Intelligent Devices and Robotics
The company rebranded its Connected Living & Digital Commerce operations as Intelligent Devices & Robotics to reflect a pivot toward automation and complex engineered solutions. Within this segment, Commerce & Robotics is expected to deliver about $3 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, up roughly 11%, fueled by retailer and warehouse investment in robotic systems and automated fulfillment.
Robotics Production and Physical AI Capabilities
Jabil’s customer Symbotic reached 10,000 bots as of June 2025 and is closing in on 20,000 units, demonstrating the scale of automated warehouse deployments. Jabil is also applying its know-how in optics, robotics, precision mechanics, sensors and thermal solutions to humanoid robots and industrial automation, laying the groundwork for broader physical AI applications.
Investments in Operational Automation and Factory Efficiency
Management is investing heavily in factory automation, material movement, computer vision and automated optical inspection to enhance manufacturing performance. These physical AI capabilities are designed to improve consistency, speed up program ramps, detect issues earlier and make equipment more reusable, boosting productivity and resilience as demand shifts.
Robust Cash Flow and Asset-Light Discipline
Cash from operations reached $733 million in the quarter and about $2 billion for fiscal 2026, while net capital expenditures remained modest at $470 million, or 1.3% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5 billion, and Jabil expects net capex of 1.5% to 2% of revenue in fiscal 2027, with adjusted free cash flow around $1.6 billion, underscoring its asset-light approach.
Structural Improvement in Profitability and Returns
Since fiscal 2020, Jabil has steadily improved its profitability, lifting core operating margin from 3.2% to 5.8% and gross margin by more than 200 basis points to 9.2%. Net capital spending has dropped from 2.9% to 1.3% of revenue, annual free cash flow has more than tripled to $1.5 billion and core ROIC has nearly tripled to 59%, signaling stronger returns on invested capital.
Strong Balance Sheet and Shareholder-Friendly Policy
The company ended fiscal 2026 with debt to core EBITDA of 1.3x, cash of about $1.7 billion and total liquidity of $6.1 billion, including $4.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity. Jabil repurchased around $1.1 billion of shares during the year, has cut its share count by 49% since 2013 and is working under a new $1.5 billion buyback plan, aiming to return at least 80% of adjusted free cash flow to investors over time.
Segment-Level Challenges and Strategic Trade-Offs
Not all areas met expectations, with healthcare and packaging revenue falling short in the quarter due to delayed automation equipment and program timing. Connected Living & Digital Commerce revenue was roughly flat year-over-year at $1.4 billion and is projected to decline about 15% to $2.3 billion in fiscal 2027, outweighing Commerce & Robotics growth and leaving Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 2% overall.
Prioritizing Profitability in Intelligent Devices & Robotics
The Intelligent Devices & Robotics segment is expected to generate about $1.2 billion in first-quarter revenue, down roughly 10% year-over-year as Jabil shifts focus from volume to returns. Management said it has exited or deemphasized lower-margin programs that failed to meet its hurdle rates, accepting near-term top-line pressure to safeguard segment profitability.
Inventory Management and Supply Constraints
Net inventory days improved by about four days sequentially to 64, though still above the target range of 55 to 60 days, reflecting higher commodity prices and greater deposits tied to cloud infrastructure. Memory supply is being redirected toward AI and hyperscale demand, and Jabil expects to navigate ongoing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions, acknowledging potential bumps as fiscal 2027 unfolds.
Ramp-Related Margin Pressure and Seasonal Headwinds
Management cautioned that fiscal 2027 revenue will be weighted 45% to the first half and 55% to the second half, with income more back-end loaded as new programs ramp. Initial ramp costs, lower yields and underutilization could compress margins in the first half, while the broader communications market remains subdued and second-quarter revenue faces typical post-holiday seasonality.
Despite heavy investment in physical AI, management noted that real-world deployments remain minimal, particularly in Western markets. Jabil has built a modest, conservative physical AI forecast into its fiscal 2027 outlook, viewing the space as a longer-term opportunity rather than a near-term growth engine.
Monitoring External Macro and Regulatory Risks
The company continues to monitor geopolitical tensions, inflation, supply-chain issues and potential regulatory changes that could affect operations. While no major regulatory disruption is assumed in fiscal 2027, Jabil remains cautious about possible inflection points tied to upcoming elections and broader macro uncertainty.
Guidance Highlights: Strong Growth, Margin Expansion
For the first quarter, Jabil expects total revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion, with Regulated Industries up about 12%, Intelligent Infrastructure up roughly 63% and Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 10%. For fiscal 2027, the company guides to revenue of about $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin of 6.1%, core EPS of $17.55, adjusted free cash flow near $1.6 billion and net capex at 1.5% to 2% of revenue.
Jabil’s latest earnings call painted the picture of a company riding a powerful AI and infrastructure wave while steadily tightening its capital and cost discipline. Despite near-term margin and segment pressures, management’s confident guidance, structural profitability gains and ongoing shareholder returns will likely keep the stock on the radar of investors seeking exposure to the hardware backbone of the AI boom.

Electronics manufacturing services provider Jabil (NYSE: JBL) reported calendar Q3 2026 (fiscal Q4 2026) results exceeding the market’s revenue expectations, with sales up 28.6% year on year to $10.62 billion. On top of that, next quarter’s revenue guidance ($11 billion at the midpoint) was surprisingly good and 9.9% above what analysts were expecting. Its non-GAAP profit of $4.40 per share was 8% above analysts’ consensus estimates.
Is now the time to buy Jabil? Find out by accessing our full research report, it’s free.
Jabil (JBL) Q3 CY2026 Highlights:
Revenue: $10.62 billion vs analyst estimates of $9.66 billion (28.6% year-on-year growth, 9.8% beat)
Adjusted EPS: $4.40 vs analyst estimates of $4.08 (8% beat)
Revenue Guidance for Q4 CY2026 is $11 billion at the midpoint, above analyst estimates of $10.01 billion
Adjusted EPS guidance for the upcoming financial year 2027 is $17.55 at the midpoint, beating analyst estimates by 3.8%
Operating Margin: 5.7%, up from 4.1% in the same quarter last year
Free Cash Flow Margin: 5.1%, down from 6.1% in the same quarter last year
With manufacturing facilities spanning the globe from China to Mexico to the United States, Jabil (NYSE: JBL) provides electronics design, manufacturing, and supply chain solutions to companies across various industries, from healthcare to automotive to cloud computing.
Reviewing a company’s long-term sales performance reveals insights into its quality. Any business can have short-term success, but a top-tier one grows for years.
With $35.95 billion in revenue over the past 12 months, Jabil is a behemoth in the business services sector and benefits from economies of scale, giving it an edge in distribution. This also enables it to gain more leverage on its fixed costs than smaller competitors and the flexibility to offer lower prices. However, its scale is a double-edged sword because it’s harder to find incremental growth when you’ve penetrated most of the market. For Jabil to boost its sales, it likely needs to adjust its prices, launch new offerings, or lean into foreign markets.
As you can see below, Jabil’s sales grew at a mediocre 4.2% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years. This shows it couldn’t generate demand in any major way and is a tough (but perhaps misleading) starting point for our analysis.
We at StockStory place the most emphasis on long-term growth, but within business services, a half-decade historical view may miss recent innovations or disruptive industry trends. Jabil’s annualized revenue growth of 11.6% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, suggesting its demand recently accelerated.
This quarter, Jabil reported robust year-on-year revenue growth of 28.6%, and its $10.62 billion of revenue topped Wall Street estimates by 9.8%. Company management is currently guiding for a 32.5% year-on-year increase in sales next quarter.
Looking further ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 19% over the next 12 months, an improvement versus the last two years. This projection is eye-popping for a company of its scale and indicates its newer products and services will fuel better top-line performance.

Adjusted operating margin is one of the best measures of profitability because it tells us how much money a company takes home after subtracting all core expenses, like marketing and R&D. It also removes various one-time costs to paint a better picture of normalized profits.
Jabil was profitable over the last five years but held back by its large cost base. Its average adjusted operating margin of 5.3% was weak for a business services business.
On the plus side, Jabil’s adjusted operating margin rose by 1.3 percentage points over the last five years, as its sales growth gave it operating leverage.
In Q3, Jabil generated an adjusted operating margin profit margin of 6.8%, in line with the same quarter last year. This indicates the company’s overall cost structure has been relatively stable.
Revenue trends explain a company’s historical growth, but the long-term change in earnings per share (EPS) points to the profitability of that growth — for example, a company could inflate its sales through excessive spending on advertising and promotions.
Jabil’s EPS grew at 18.5% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years, higher than its 4.2% annualized revenue growth. This tells us the company became more profitable on a per-share basis as it expanded.
We can take a deeper look into Jabil’s earnings quality to better understand the drivers of its performance. As we mentioned earlier, Jabil’s adjusted operating margin was flat this quarter but expanded by 1.3 percentage points over the last five years. On top of that, its share count shrank by 29.4%. These are positive signs for shareholders because improving profitability and share buybacks turbocharge EPS growth relative to revenue growth.
Like with revenue, we analyze EPS over a shorter period to see if we are missing a change in the business.
For Jabil, its two-year annual EPS growth of 24.4% was higher than its five-year trend. We love it when earnings growth accelerates, especially when it accelerates off an already high base.
In Q3, Jabil reported adjusted EPS of $4.40, up from $3.29 in the same quarter last year. This print beat analysts’ estimates by 8%. Over the next 12 months, Wall Street expects Jabil’s full-year EPS to grow 28.7% from $13.10 to $16.85.
We were impressed by how significantly Jabil blew past analysts’ EPS guidance for next quarter expectations this quarter. We were also excited its revenue outperformed Wall Street’s estimates by a wide margin. Zooming out, we think this was a good print with some key areas of upside. The market seemed to be hoping for more, and the stock traded down 2.8% to $310.01 immediately after reporting.
Is Jabil an attractive investment opportunity right now? What happened in the latest quarter matters, but not as much as longer-term business quality and valuation, when deciding whether to invest in this stock. What Is the Market Really Paying for Jabil’s (JBL) Growth?
Jabil (NYSE:JBL) has evolved into a high-margin advanced manufacturing powerhouse, shifting away from low-margin assembly toward AI infrastructure, healthcare, and high-complexity hardware. The company's underlying fundamentals highlight exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by a core return on invested capital that expanded to 59% in fiscal 2026 while sustaining aggressive share repurchases. Even as Jabil expands its footprint, could a major rival's massive multi-billion-dollar play in AI power infrastructure siphon market share away? Click to find out.
What Is the Market Really Paying for Jabil's (JBL) Growth?
Jabil has spent years shedding its image as a plain contract manufacturer, and its Sept. 30, 2026 earnings call made the case that the makeover is paying off. Fourth-quarter revenue jumped 29% year over year, and core earnings per share rose 34% to $4.40. Management then guided fiscal 2027 core EPS to $17.55, another gain of about 34%. The business is clearly accelerating, but what investors are willing to pay for that acceleration is the more interesting story. Yet, as hardware demand surges across hyperscale networks, will another key supplier steal the spotlight in optical connectivity after a major sector giant's recent plunge? Read more here.
The engine is AI infrastructure. Jabil generated $14.4 billion of AI-related revenue in fiscal 2026 and expects $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, a 54% increase. What makes that easier to believe is where the demand comes from. Management says most of it supports inference, the everyday running of existing models, rather than the race to train frontier systems, and direct exposure to frontier developers is a small fraction. Usage-driven demand needs storage, networking, power, and cooling, not just accelerators, and Jabil now builds across all of it. Six customers in the segment are expected to top $1 billion each in fiscal 2027.
The second leg is how efficiently growth turns into cash. Jabil supported $36.0 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026 on just $470 million of net capital spending, which is why core return on invested capital sits at 59%, nearly triple the fiscal 2020 level. Free cash flow beat the company's own early target, and management plans to return at least 80% of it to shareholders over time. Buybacks absorbed about $1.1 billion of that in fiscal 2026.
Growth at this pace has to be physically built, and supply is the choke point. Francis McKay, the chief supply chain officer, said memory is being pulled toward AI and hyperscale buyers, squeezing the other markets Jabil serves. That already shows up in guidance, where Connected Living is expected to shrink 15% to $2.3 billion, partly because management is cautious about memory and partly because it is exiting lower-complexity programs. Healthcare also fell short of expectations in the fourth quarter, thanks to equipment delays and a customer program that slipped.
Execution and concentration come next. Jabil is adding more than $8.5 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, which management itself called unprecedented, and a second hyperscale customer is expected to pass 10% of total revenue, a mark only one customer reached two years ago. Net inventory days of 64 still sit above the 55 to 60 day target, so working capital has to tighten while the factories scale. Management also raised the question of AI volatility on the call, arguing that its inference-heavy mix is steadier.
Hedge fund interest ticked higher, with 69 funds holding Jabil against 67 in the prior quarter, so institutions are adding rather than heading for the exits. Short interest of 3.24% of float is low, which signals little organized betting against the story. The forward P/E of 19.34, as of October 2, is where the real debate sits. Earnings are guided to grow about 34% in fiscal 2027, so a multiple under 20 leaves little growth premium in the price, and the market appears to want proof before paying for it. Is that caution fair? An inference-heavy mix and a share count cut by 49% since fiscal 2013 argue for some support under the stock. But a modest multiple only looks cheap if the earnings arrive, and memory supply and the capacity buildout are the two things that could delay them.
Jabil's story comes down to whether its new factory space fills on schedule. The evidence shows a company growing fast, generating cash and trading at a multiple that does not demand perfection. Bulls need committed customer programs to keep ramping into the capacity already built. Bears need only a memory shortage or a stumbled launch to show how much.
While we acknowledge the potential of JBL as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. Jabil’s Double-Beat and Raise Is a Signal That This Rally Will Continue
Thomas Hughes - MarketBeat - Thu Oct 1, 8:45AM CDT
Tepid market response or not, Jabil’s (NYSE: JBL) recent double-beat earnings report was a buy signal, reinforcing the thesis that has driven shares thus far and strengthening the forward outlook.
AI is driving a surge in demand across the company's product lines, pointing to a sustained upcycle and cash-generating capacity.
Cash-generating capacity is the core thesis, as Jabil is the muscle behind more prominent names such as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), and Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ), converting demand for their products into reality.
Jabil’s dividend is a token, yielding less than 0.25%, intended mainly to keep dividend-only funds and institutions in the mix. The firm aggressively repurchases shares and can continue doing so next year.
Highlights from its last fiscal year include about $1 billion in repurchases, up year over year and sufficient to reduce the share count by 3.6%, and a free cash flow payout ratio of about 69%.
Looking ahead, management forecasts free cash flow growth in the coming year, signaling capacity for accelerated buybacks and greater shareholder leverage, which may provide an incentive to buy shares at current levels.
Jabil Boosted by AI, Shows Strengths in All Categories
Jabil posted a solid quarter, with revenue accelerating sequentially and year over year (YOY) to nearly 29%, the fastest pace in more than five years. Revenue growth also outpaced the consensus by a wide margin, approximately 900 basis points (bps), driven by 56% growth in Intelligent Infrastructure. Intelligent Infrastructure did the heavy lifting, but was not the only segment to show strength, with Regulated Industries up by 9% and Connected Living/Digital Commerce flat. CEO Mike Dastoor also highlighted several end markets not related to the data center and AI infrastructure, including automotive, healthcare, energy, defense, aerospace, and warehouse automation.
Margin news was another bright spot. The company faced cost pressures and gross margin headwinds, but they were less than expected and offset by operational quality. Selling, general, and administrative expenses increased at a much slower pace than revenue growth, showing that Jabil is becoming more efficient as it grows, which helped earnings rise faster than revenue. Adjusted earnings per share rose nearly 34% YOY to $4.40, outpacing top-line growth by about 500 bps, with strengths expected to carry into the coming year.
Guidance is a key reason the stock price uptrend is likely to continue. Jabil’s guidance for the next quarter and year is hot on all counts, with revenue and earnings expected to be well above MarketBeat’s reported consensus. The likely outcome is that JBL continues to build momentum, running at the high end of its expected range if not exceeding it, and lifting the year-end outlook along the way.
Analysts Caution Triggers Buying Opportunity in Jabil Shares
Analysts were generally bullish following Jabil’s release, highlighting the revenue strength and earnings quality, but took a cautious stance, focusing on back-end margin expansion and the upfront cost of its capacity buildout. No analysts revised a price target or altered sentiment immediately following the report, leaving the trend unchanged.
The trend includes steady coverage, a Buy consensus with 90% Buy-side bias, and a forecast for nearly 50% upside relative to Q3’s support levels and a fresh all-time high. More importantly, JBL trades well below the lowest analyst price target, signaling a deep-value opportunity and potential for explosive upside as stronger catalysts emerge.
Institutions are likewise bullish on Jabil's stock, citing its cash flow, capital returns, and underlying demand for its clients' products. They own more than 90% of the shares, have bought aggressively over the trailing 12 months, and ramped activity in Q3, reaching a record peak.
JBL’s price action reflects a bullish market posture. The stock is up more than 35% YOY and more than 100% over the past two years, with the 2026 pullback offering value relative to recent peaks. A deeper pullback is possible, but strong support is evident as September comes to a close, so the risk is minimal. The likely scenario is that JBL remains close to this level until more news becomes available, likely in upcoming earnings reports.
The market may not be getting JBL’s report wrong so much as the price action reflects the split between short-term traders and long-term investors. Short-term traders focus on near-term bottlenecks, AI fears, and capacity costs, and fail to price in the impact on long-term cash flow. Long-term traders, focused on cash flow, capital returns, and capital gains, can easily look past upfront costs and focus on the demand curve, which is improving quarterly across numerous end markets, not just AI.
Jabil’s biggest risk now is executional. Investors need the company's strategy to progress without hiccups, which are likely, given the advanced nature of AI hardware and industry-wide bottlenecks.

Jabil Inc. Earnings Call: AI Boom Fuels 2027 Outlook
Tipranks - Tipranks - Fri Oct 2, 7:08PM CDT
Jabil Inc. ((JBL)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Jabil Inc. struck a decidedly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call as management showcased record fourth-quarter execution and robust growth plans stretching into fiscal 2027. Executives acknowledged pockets of softness and operational friction, yet emphasized accelerating AI demand, improving margins and strong free cash flow as key drivers of confidence in the company’s long-term trajectory.
Fourth-Quarter Surge in Revenue and Earnings
Jabil delivered a powerful finish to fiscal 2026, with fourth-quarter revenue around $10.6 billion, up 29% year-over-year and more than $1 billion above its June outlook midpoint. Core operating income reached $675 million and core diluted EPS climbed 34% to $4.40, with both revenue and EPS surpassing the high end of guidance, underscoring strong execution across the portfolio.
Fiscal 2026: Broad-Based Growth and Cash Generation
For the full year, revenue grew 21% and core operating margin expanded by 40 basis points, signaling better pricing, mix and efficiency. Core EPS increased 34%, while adjusted free cash flow exceeded $1.5 billion, up more than $200 million, reinforcing the benefits of Jabil’s asset-light manufacturing model and disciplined capital spending.
Intelligent Infrastructure Drives Outperformance
Intelligent Infrastructure was the standout segment in the quarter, posting revenue of roughly $5.8 billion, up 56% year-over-year and about $900 million ahead of June expectations. Management highlighted that AI-related demand is not only strong but accelerating, as capacity came online faster than planned and customer ramps progressed better than anticipated.
Margin Improvement in Intelligent Infrastructure
Core operating margin in Intelligent Infrastructure reached 6.5%, an increase of 60 basis points from a year earlier. This improvement reflects a more favorable business mix and contribution from the Hanley Energy acquisition, which management described as margin-accretive and strategically aligned with Jabil’s data center and power solutions.
Rapid Expansion and Diversification of AI Revenue
AI-related revenue hit approximately $14.4 billion in fiscal 2026, rising $5.4 billion from the prior year as hyperscale and cloud customers stepped up orders. Jabil expects AI-related revenue to surge another 54% to about $22.1 billion in fiscal 2027, with four customers already above $1 billion in annual AI sales and six Intelligent Infrastructure customers forecast to exceed that threshold next year.
Broad-Based Intelligent Infrastructure Growth Outlook
Looking ahead to fiscal 2027, Intelligent Infrastructure revenue is projected at roughly $25.6 billion, about 43% higher than in 2026, with all three end markets growing at double-digit rates. Capital equipment revenue is expected to rise about 40% to $4.2 billion, cloud and data center infrastructure about 52% to $17.5 billion and networking and communications about 15% to $3.9 billion.
Global Capacity Expansion to Meet Committed Demand
To support its growth, Jabil added roughly 4 million square feet of capacity across Southeast Asia, the U.S., Mexico and India, targeting high-demand markets and strategic customers. Management stressed that committed business is already filling this footprint and that ongoing customer ramps and new capacity coming online will underpin the company’s fiscal 2027 growth trajectory.
Regulated Industries Growth and Portfolio Upgrades
Regulated Industries delivered solid growth, with fourth-quarter revenue of $3.4 billion, up 9% year-over-year and above guidance, helped by stronger automotive, transportation and energy infrastructure demand. For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects the segment to reach about $13.6 billion, up around 7%, with mid-single to high-single digit growth across automotive, healthcare, packaging and renewable energy.
Strategic Repositioning in Automotive Mix
Automotive returned to growth faster than expected, driven by stronger operational execution and better win rates with strategic customers. The business has shifted away from heavy exposure to electrification and powertrain, which fell from about 80% of the portfolio in fiscal 2023 to around 40% in fiscal 2026, with software-defined vehicles, vehicle compute and advanced driver assistance now constituting much of the balance.
Defense, Aerospace and Healthcare Build Momentum
Defense and aerospace are poised to become more meaningful contributors in fiscal 2027 as several programs transition from development into production. Healthcare is expected to resume growth as clients launch new products and engage Jabil for complex manufacturing, with the company planning to produce more than 700 million injectors and pens and ramp its Croatia facility through 2027 into full production in fiscal 2028.
Expanding Footprint in Energy Infrastructure
Renewable and energy infrastructure conditions improved through fiscal 2026, with investment expanding beyond solar into storage, grid solutions and thermal management. Jabil is channeling capital into engineering, vertical integration and selective deals in power electronics and low-voltage switchgear, positioning the company as a broader partner in decarbonization and data center cooling.
Shift Toward Intelligent Devices and Robotics
The company rebranded its Connected Living & Digital Commerce operations as Intelligent Devices & Robotics to reflect a pivot toward automation and complex engineered solutions. Within this segment, Commerce & Robotics is expected to deliver about $3 billion of revenue in fiscal 2027, up roughly 11%, fueled by retailer and warehouse investment in robotic systems and automated fulfillment.
Robotics Production and Physical AI Capabilities
Jabil’s customer Symbotic reached 10,000 bots as of June 2025 and is closing in on 20,000 units, demonstrating the scale of automated warehouse deployments. Jabil is also applying its know-how in optics, robotics, precision mechanics, sensors and thermal solutions to humanoid robots and industrial automation, laying the groundwork for broader physical AI applications.
Investments in Operational Automation and Factory Efficiency
Management is investing heavily in factory automation, material movement, computer vision and automated optical inspection to enhance manufacturing performance. These physical AI capabilities are designed to improve consistency, speed up program ramps, detect issues earlier and make equipment more reusable, boosting productivity and resilience as demand shifts.
Robust Cash Flow and Asset-Light Discipline
Cash from operations reached $733 million in the quarter and about $2 billion for fiscal 2026, while net capital expenditures remained modest at $470 million, or 1.3% of revenue. Adjusted free cash flow topped $1.5 billion, and Jabil expects net capex of 1.5% to 2% of revenue in fiscal 2027, with adjusted free cash flow around $1.6 billion, underscoring its asset-light approach.
Structural Improvement in Profitability and Returns
Since fiscal 2020, Jabil has steadily improved its profitability, lifting core operating margin from 3.2% to 5.8% and gross margin by more than 200 basis points to 9.2%. Net capital spending has dropped from 2.9% to 1.3% of revenue, annual free cash flow has more than tripled to $1.5 billion and core ROIC has nearly tripled to 59%, signaling stronger returns on invested capital.
Strong Balance Sheet and Shareholder-Friendly Policy
The company ended fiscal 2026 with debt to core EBITDA of 1.3x, cash of about $1.7 billion and total liquidity of $6.1 billion, including $4.4 billion of unused borrowing capacity. Jabil repurchased around $1.1 billion of shares during the year, has cut its share count by 49% since 2013 and is working under a new $1.5 billion buyback plan, aiming to return at least 80% of adjusted free cash flow to investors over time.
Segment-Level Challenges and Strategic Trade-Offs
Not all areas met expectations, with healthcare and packaging revenue falling short in the quarter due to delayed automation equipment and program timing. Connected Living & Digital Commerce revenue was roughly flat year-over-year at $1.4 billion and is projected to decline about 15% to $2.3 billion in fiscal 2027, outweighing Commerce & Robotics growth and leaving Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 2% overall.
Prioritizing Profitability in Intelligent Devices & Robotics
The Intelligent Devices & Robotics segment is expected to generate about $1.2 billion in first-quarter revenue, down roughly 10% year-over-year as Jabil shifts focus from volume to returns. Management said it has exited or deemphasized lower-margin programs that failed to meet its hurdle rates, accepting near-term top-line pressure to safeguard segment profitability.
Inventory Management and Supply Constraints
Net inventory days improved by about four days sequentially to 64, though still above the target range of 55 to 60 days, reflecting higher commodity prices and greater deposits tied to cloud infrastructure. Memory supply is being redirected toward AI and hyperscale demand, and Jabil expects to navigate ongoing geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions, acknowledging potential bumps as fiscal 2027 unfolds.
Ramp-Related Margin Pressure and Seasonal Headwinds
Management cautioned that fiscal 2027 revenue will be weighted 45% to the first half and 55% to the second half, with income more back-end loaded as new programs ramp. Initial ramp costs, lower yields and underutilization could compress margins in the first half, while the broader communications market remains subdued and second-quarter revenue faces typical post-holiday seasonality.
Despite heavy investment in physical AI, management noted that real-world deployments remain minimal, particularly in Western markets. Jabil has built a modest, conservative physical AI forecast into its fiscal 2027 outlook, viewing the space as a longer-term opportunity rather than a near-term growth engine.
Monitoring External Macro and Regulatory Risks
The company continues to monitor geopolitical tensions, inflation, supply-chain issues and potential regulatory changes that could affect operations. While no major regulatory disruption is assumed in fiscal 2027, Jabil remains cautious about possible inflection points tied to upcoming elections and broader macro uncertainty.
Guidance Highlights: Strong Growth, Margin Expansion
For the first quarter, Jabil expects total revenue between $10.6 billion and $11.4 billion, with Regulated Industries up about 12%, Intelligent Infrastructure up roughly 63% and Intelligent Devices & Robotics down about 10%. For fiscal 2027, the company guides to revenue of about $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin of 6.1%, core EPS of $17.55, adjusted free cash flow near $1.6 billion and net capex at 1.5% to 2% of revenue.
Jabil’s latest earnings call painted the picture of a company riding a powerful AI and infrastructure wave while steadily tightening its capital and cost discipline. Despite near-term margin and segment pressures, management’s confident guidance, structural profitability gains and ongoing shareholder returns will likely keep the stock on the radar of investors seeking exposure to the hardware backbone of the AI boom.

Jabil's Fiscal 2027 Outlook Leaves Room for Upside, UBS Says
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 9:59 AM PDT 1 min read
Jabil's (JBL) initial fiscal 2027 outlook looks cautious given management's history of guiding low and then beating, so the market is likely to underwrite higher estimates, UBS Securities said.
The brokerage said in a note Wednesday that the company started fiscal 2025 and 2026 roughly 10% and 15% above its initial revenue guides, respectively, and expects investors to assume at least 10% upside to the $44.5 billion fiscal 2027 revenue guide, or about $49 billion.
Stronger volume should also leave room for operating margin to expand 10 to 20 basis points beyond the initial 6.1% guide, UBS said. It expects the market to underwrite EPS of at least $20, versus the $17.55 guide.
The investment firm raised its fiscal 2027 earnings per share estimate to $17.57 from $16.78 and its fiscal 2028 estimate to $22.63 from $20.24. It cited stronger AI-related demand. Jabil also raised its fiscal 2027 AI-related revenue growth outlook to 54% from about 50%.
UBS kept its buy rating and $430 price target.
Shares of Jabil were up 3.4% in Thursday afternoon trading.

Jabil Posts Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026 Results
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – September 30, 2026 –Today, Jabil Inc. (NYSE: JBL), reported preliminary, unaudited financial results for its fourth quarter and fiscal year ended August 31, 2026.
“We delivered a fourth quarter that exceeded our expectations, closing an exceptional fiscal 2026 in which we grew revenue 21%, expanded core operating margin 40 basis points and generated more than $1.5 billion in adjusted free cash flow,” said CEO Mike Dastoor. “Our teams supported significant growth in AI infrastructure, delivered strong performance across several other end markets and brought critical new capacity online. These results reflect the progress we’ve made in moving up the value chain, taking on more of our customers’ engineering and manufacturing complexity while maintaining an asset-light model. I’m proud of our teams and the stronger business we’re building together.”
Fourth Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026 Highlights:
•U.S. GAAP operating income: $602 million
•U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share: $3.76
•Core operating income (Non-GAAP): $675 million
•Core diluted earnings per share (Non-GAAP): $4.40
Fiscal Year 2026 Highlights:
•U.S. GAAP operating income: $1.7 billion
•U.S. GAAP diluted earnings per share: $9.75
•Core operating income (Non-GAAP): $2.1 billion
•Core diluted earnings per share (Non-GAAP): $13.09
First Quarter of Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook:
•Core diluted earnings per share (Non-GAAP)(1)
(1)Core operating income and core diluted earnings per share exclude anticipated adjustments of $24 million for amortization of intangibles (or $0.21 per diluted share) and $62 million for stock-based compensation expense and related charges (or $0.58 per diluted share) and $25 million (or $0.23 per diluted share) for restructuring, severance and related charges.
“Our fiscal 2027 outlook reflects the strength of Jabil’s diversified portfolio, with accelerating AI demand complemented by solid growth in automotive, healthcare, energy infrastructure, defense and aerospace, and warehouse and retail automation,” Dastoor continued. “This breadth of growth, together with expanding customer relationships and committed business supporting our new capacity, gives us confidence in the year ahead. We expect revenue of $44.5 billion, up 24%, core operating margin expansion of 30 basis points to 6.1%, core diluted earnings per share growth of 34% to $17.55, and adjusted free cash flow of approximately $1.6 billion. As customers turn to Jabil for more of their engineering, supply chain and manufacturing needs, we see significant opportunities to sustain profitable growth, invest in our capabilities and return substantial capital to shareholders.”
Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook:
•Core diluted earnings per share (Non-GAAP)

Jabil defines core earnings as core operating income, less loss on debt extinguishment, loss (gain) on securities, other components of net periodic benefit cost, income (loss) from discontinued operations, gain (loss) on sale of discontinued operations and certain other expenses, net of tax and certain deferred tax valuation allowance charges. Jabil defines adjusted free cash flow as net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less net capital expenditures (acquisition of property, plant and equipment less proceeds and advances from sale of property, plant and equipment).
